messages:
alana: Kicking off a preflight for the new multi-org accounts. TL;DR — need GPU quota bump (T4/P4 or equivalent), VPC network quota (regional IPs + routes), IAM roles, billing export, and tagging policy. Posting a checklist so we can assign owners and open quota requests.

alana: Checklist (quick):
• Create org + projects: infra-prod, infra-staging, infra-dev
• Billing account linked and billing export to infra-billing-prod (BigQuery)
• IAM: infra-admin group + least-priv svc accounts for autoscaler
• Tags: env, team, cost-center, project-owner
• GPU quotas: request per-region GPU core quota + specific gpu-type quotas (n1-standard fallback)
• Networking: regional external IP quota, routes limit, VPC peering limits
• SCC/org policies: enforce org-level labels and disable public bucket ACLs

alana: Who can own the AWS/Azure quota requests? I can take GCP.

mike: I can own AWS. Quick Q: which instance families? We should aim for p4d-lite where available, otherwise fallback to g4dn/p3. Also set soft and hard limits: request soft first, set hard if we need committed capacity later.

raj: For GCP quotas, open a request for both "GPUs (all regions)" and per-region "GPUs (e.g., us-west1)". Include expected baseline usage: 50 GPUs month1, 200 month3. Tag the request with ticket: INFRA-4729.

raj: CLI snippet to check current quotas:```bash
gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --project=infra-prod --format="json(quotas)" | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'
```This saved me last time when quotas looked fine but per-zone was zero.

priya: I'll own Azure. Note: we need to pre-request regional vCPUs + Accelerated Networking NIC quotas in the subscript. Also create a billing scope and link subscription to Cost Management export. I'll add the tag policy to the policy repo and share the PR.

quota-bot: Quota check report (automated): GCP infra-prod: GPUs 8/50 (us-west1), external IPs 32/32 (us-west1) — external IPs at capacity. AWS prod: ElasticIPs 5/5 in us-west-2. Azure prod: AcceleratedNICs 0/100.

mike: Uh — external IPs at capacity in GCP is a blocker for initial rollout. Options: request increase, use Cloud NAT, or reserve static IPs in a different region and failover. Thoughts?

alana: Let's open a ticket for immediate external IP increase and simultaneously provision a Cloud NAT as a short-term fix. Raj — please include the Cloud NAT plan in the GCP request so support knows it's time-sensitive.

raj: On it. I'll attach expected time window and traffic profile. Also recommending IP quota increase + route quota bump (we currently have 200 routes limit in infra-prod).

priya: For Azure, I'll schedule the NIC quota bump and create tags: {env,team,costcenter,owner} in policy. I'll also add alerting to the billing export for anomalous spend to /ops-billing.

mike: For AWS EIPs, I can consolidate some old stacks to free up 10 EIPs then request soft increase to 50. Will create ticket INFRA-4734 and link here.

alana: Owners: GCP=raj, AWS=mike, Azure=priya. Follow-ups:
• raj: open GCP quota ticket + include Cloud NAT fallback (due EOD)
• mike: cleanup EIPs + open AWS quota ticket (due EOD)
• priya: open Azure NIC quota ticket + push tagging policy PR (due EOD)

alana: Also note: tagging must be enforced at create-time via org constraints; don't rely on post-hoc labeling. If anyone needs help with constraint policy examples I can paste a sample.

raj: Sample policy snippet for GCP org constraint (we used this before):```yaml
constraint: constraints/gcp.resourceLocations
allowedValues:
  - in:us-west1
  - in:us-central1
```Will paste full PR shortly.

mike: I'll update the runbook with fallback region mapping and instance-family substitutions.

priya: Adding billing alerts: threshold 10k/day notify #ops-billing and pager duty.

alana: Thanks team — ping me in thread when tickets are created and paste the support case IDs. We'll run the quota-checker again after increases. :thumbsup:

quota-bot: Reminder scheduled: Re-run quota scan in 3 hours and post results.
